# Review — secret-history-158-164

## Pass 1

Adversarial reviewer, pass 1. `units.json` edited in place by script (backup of the draft kept in the scratchpad). `t` (all 509 words, in order, each used exactly once, each equal to the packet word) is unchanged; only cut points moved (64 units to 55). `ln` and `p: true` verified on the first unit of each of §§158–164; every unit has `l`, `i`, `n` and a `words` entry per word with non-empty morphs.

Entries by severity (an entry may cover several units): major 1, moderate 8, minor 14, trivial 13.

Unit numbers are the new numbering unless marked 'old' (the draft's 0–63). Merges: old 5+6 = new 5; 7+8 = 6; 20+21 = 18; 22+23+24 = 19; 28+29 = 23; 35+36 = 29; 45+46 = 38; 54+55 = 46; every other old unit n = new n minus (merges before it): old 9 = 7 … old 19 = 17, old 25 = 20, old 32 = 26, old 37 = 30, old 44 = 37, old 56 = 47, old 63 = 54.

## Findings refused

- Old 0 'Naiman Köchügüd' and old 40 'my four heroes / my own son's people' (min-u beside a reflexive): the readings are doubtful, but the notes already say so and the English follows the Mongol word for word; nothing sounder is available from the glosses. Kept.
- Old 1 'When they reached him at ...' for büküi-dür kürčü: a smoothing, but the note states the first reading ('Buiruγ Qān was at the river'). Kept.
- Old 8/9 `boldažu` labelled passive in the morph but 'having become' in `l`: the Ming 被做着 is passive, English 'when evening fell / was gone' is the natural sense and the note says so. Kept.
- Old 31 active 'The Naiman have plundered me of ...' for the passive daγ̇uliγdaba: same force, noted in `l`. Kept.
- Old 32 and 37 'give them back': 'back' is not in ögbe/ögtügei, but it is the sense of the sequence and the note says so; the 154–157 and earlier parts do the same. Kept.
- Old 48–49 ('on the heights ... on the crags'), 51, 61, 63 (figurative lines): the notes already say the glosses give only the words; I found no overclaim beyond what is flagged. 'in close friendship they passed their time together' (old 63) supplies an object for alduba, which the note admits; English needs one. Kept.
- Old 19 (Kürin's retort) and old 17 (Jamuqa's accusation): both rest on Ming glosses and are marked first readings; kept.
- Old 24 'going by the way already travelled': kept as a stated reading (see the trivial row).
- Old 6/26 'epithet or plural noun' for Naiman-u qadqulduγči: kept as the note states it.
- `bi-jü` split as bi- + -jü (glossary: bijü as a present form): the draft's two-morph analysis is a defensible reading and the lemma is the glossary's bü-/bi- stem. Kept.
- Other long chains (old 0/1, 2/3, 26/27, 35/37, 56–58): kept cut as readable, as in 154–157.

## Remaining doubts

- §160 bird figure: which birds, and what staying/going means, is unexplained; the English now says only 'bird'.
- Old 21–22 tülešilen (§161) and old 46 ken-ü emüne (§164): not understood; the English is a shaping.
- §163 speeches: who the 'son' is in the first speech (Senggum most likely), and the 'my four heroes' beside 'my own son's people'.
- §164 last unit: what alduba passes (time?), and amaγ̇aralin; the 'father-and-son pledge' unit's grammar (the principle clause is open).
- Stems inferred from the Ming alone: aisu-, baildu-, jada-, dutaγ̇a-, žusurid-, ažira-, qaγ-, qaγ̇ul-, olulča-, araγ̇a, -γ̇ul- in daba-γ̇ulun.
- Pass 2 (with gloss.json) still to check: the glossary entries for the new forms, especially birds, tülešilen, γ̇ulun and abur-i.
